results.notes: Sources: saved working-paper PDF pp. 14, 16, and 23 (printed pp. 11, 13, and 20), Tables 1, 2, and 5; read the complete 119358-character markdown, including Appendices A-C. Numeric cells checked against PDF page text. All table means, SDs, coefficients, and SEs are compared at three decimals; counts are compared exactly. The Figshare and Mendeley deposits contain the same 360 participants and identical values in all 57 shared columns, verified after aligning id_prog; the deposits are not pooled. Both DTA files match their manifest SHA-256 hashes. id_prog and id_code are complete and unique. All deposited participants have all three outcomes and are retained, including those assigned AI who made no queries. No additional exclusions are applied. Original randomized counts and exclusions before deposition remain unknown. Outcome: mean of grade_1, grade_2, grade_3, and grade_4 within each participant in Mendeley v2. This equals grade_mean exactly for all 360 participants in both deposits. Each person contributes one composition; SDs are across participant means, with denominator n-1. Comparison: T_AI, PR_AI, and LOT_AI versus T_NoAI, PR_NoAI, and LOT_NoAI. Reproduction uses Table 5 OLS with intercept, AI, tournament, and piece-rate indicators, with Lottery omitted, and HC1 covariance to reproduce Stata's robust SE. The requested computed.difference is the unadjusted participant-weighted mean difference, estimated by OLS on intercept and AI alone; it is not the adjusted Table 5 coefficient. Session uncertainty: the paper states random assignment but does not explicitly identify whether people or sessions were randomized. The deposited session variable has 21 distinct values and every session contains exactly one treatment arm. PDF p. 8 refers to sessions conducted under a treatment, and Appendix A instructions (PDF p. 30) apply the same rules to everyone in the session. Therefore this analysis uses session-clustered uncertainty for the observed treatment delivery structure; this is an analytical decision, not confirmation of the unreported allocation protocol. This contrast contains 12 AI sessions and 9 no-AI sessions; n_clusters is their observed total, not a claimed randomized count. CR1 covariance uses sum_g[(X_g' u_g)(X_g' u_g)'] between two (X'X)^(-1) matrices, multiplied by G/(G-1)*(N-1)/(N-K), with K=2. Participant means and SDs weight people equally; session means are not used as outcomes. Three recorded sessions contain 24 participants, despite the paper saying sessions had up to 20; recorded session IDs are retained without speculative splitting. The six arms each contain 3 no-AI or 4 AI sessions. Between-subjects design: round=all refers to the single writing task and its post-task questionnaire. Later stages reuse the same writing; there is no paired AI/no-AI outcome or first-round crossover result. No across-person diversity estimate occurs in the reconciled extraction. The deposited Stata programs were consulted only as text.
